metric_model: CHAOSS AI Alignment - Community Governed Use

scope.note: Scoring confined to the files named on the command line; 'no' means not addressed in those files.

domains.scope_or_volume_limits: Disclosure triggered when AI is used 'for substantive portions of the contribution'; otherwise no explicit volume limit.
domains.accountability_holder: Contributors ('Contributors are responsible for all submitted content...')

evidence.quote: Contributors are responsible for all submitted content, regardless of whether generative AI tools were used.
If generative AI tools were used for substantive portions of the contribution, contributors must describe their use in the change description.
Contributors are expected to actively engage with reviewer feedback themselves.

domains.reasoning: The policy explicitly names code contributions (PRs), states a disclosure requirement tied to substantive AI use, requires contributors to be able to explain and engage with changes (human-in-the-loop elements), and names contributors as accountable for submitted content. Both supervision level and accountability holder are stated, so this domain is fully addressed.

domains.suggested_improvement: no mention of meeting/notetaker bots at all
domains.reasoning: The policy text contains no reference to meeting recording, transcription, or notetaker bots of any kind.

domains.scope_or_volume_limits: Documentation and comments are mentioned only as examples for style consistency, not as a scoped rule.

evidence.quote: this particularly means conveying information (comments, documentation, etc) in a style the Astropy community uses, and that is appropriate and to the point.

domains.suggested_improvement: no supervision level or accountability holder for documentation/content
domains.reasoning: Documentation and comments are named explicitly, but only in the context of matching community writing style - no supervision level, accountability holder, or disclosure rule specific to content/documentation/blogs/design assets is stated. This is a named-but-incomplete case.

domains.suggested_improvement: no mention of AI use in moderation actions
domains.reasoning: The policy does not discuss moderation actions (e.g., using AI to flag, warn, or ban community members) at all.

domains.suggested_improvement: no rule on whether reviewers may use AI to review
domains.reasoning: The policy discusses contributor obligations during review (explaining changes, engaging with feedback) but never addresses whether maintainers/reviewers themselves may use AI tools to conduct review. That is a distinct, unaddressed question.

domains.scope_or_volume_limits: Applies to autonomous workflows/agents submitting or acting as contributors; a human controlling the account must be available to interact with reviewers.

evidence.quote: Autonomous workflows ("agents") are not human contributors. Astropy reviewers expect to interact with the human controlling the account, or we will close the PR.

domains.reasoning: The policy explicitly names autonomous agentic workflows, states they are not accepted as contributors in their own right (effectively banning unsupervised agentic submission), and names the human controlling the account as the accountable party reviewers must interact with. Note the 'we will close the PR' clause is enforcement, but the requirement to interact with 'the human controlling the account' independently states who is answerable for the output, satisfying the accountability element.

domains.suggested_improvement: no mention of energy, water, or hardware/carbon footprint
domains.reasoning: The policy contains no discussion, rule, or rationale referencing environmental impact of AI tools.

domains.suggested_improvement: no mention of infrastructure or server-load strain from AI
domains.reasoning: No text addresses infrastructure cost, server load, or hardware financing concerns related to AI use.

domains.suggested_improvement: no mention of training data provenance or platform user data
domains.reasoning: The policy addresses licensing compliance of submitted code but never discusses the provenance or consent status of data used to train generative AI models, nor use of platform/community data for training.

unscoped_statements.quote: The following apply to all contributions.
Contributors are responsible for all submitted content, regardless of whether generative AI tools were used.

consent_policy_specificity.overall_posture: The policy is fairly specific about code contributions (disclosure for substantive AI use, mandatory human explanation/engagement, contributor accountability) and explicitly bans treating autonomous agents as contributors, but it is silent on notetaker bots, moderation, reviewer-side AI use, environmental impact, infrastructure strain, and training-data provenance, and only glancingly touches documentation/content as a style example without setting supervision or accountability for it.

awaiting_implementation.specific_tools_in_use: Awaiting implementation: named-product detection beyond known file signatures
awaiting_implementation.ai_tool_owner: Awaiting implementation: ownership and data control
awaiting_implementation.environmental_footprint: Awaiting implementation: model/system card and ESG disclosure
awaiting_implementation.proportionality: Awaiting implementation: resource use relative to contributor count (needs platform usage data)

use_composition_partial.note: Detection only. Absence of signal is not absence of use.

policy_change.blocker: Draft classifier not wired in or validated against hand-graded history. Repo.history() and Repo.commit_patch() supply the diffs.

use_compliance.blocker: Derived metric. Requires disclosed-use data (Use Composition) checked against the specificity grid. Composition is only partially detectable, so the comparison is not yet sound.

misuse.blocker: Not automatable. CHAOSS marks the core signals unknown: text-based AI detectors are unreliable, and license-laundering and wrongful-accusation incidents need maintainer self-report.
